notes: Zone pd_water: the two ponds as level water. Level 98.61 m (NAVD88) for both: the median of the LiDAR's water returns (class 9) inside each traced shore, 98.61 in the north pond (6,269 returns, 5th to 95th percentile 98.58 to 98.84) and 98.61 in the south pond (1,182, 98.57 to 98.89); the few ground returns on the water agree (98.61 and 98.63). Shores traced on the LiDAR, not the ortho: in the 2020 ortho trees hang over most of the shore and the water under them cannot be told from the bank. A 0.5 m cell is water where it has a water return, ground under 98.72 m (0.11 m over the level), or no ground return and no ground under 99.2 m within 1 m; the cells were opened (two cells) and closed (three) to drop noise, the two bodies traced, held 1.5 m inside the footprint, simplified to 1.2 m and every corner rounded with the largest true arc up to 6 m that leaves 55 % of each run straight. The two bodies are parted by the wooded spit, whose ground stands 98.9 to 99.05 m. OSM's two ponds (ways 233913170, 233913228) lie off these shores by a median of 1.5 m (north; up to 8.8 m) and 4.5 m (south; up to 15 m), and the south one runs on south-east up a slope the LiDAR shows dry (100 to 123 m), so they are not used. Trees standing in the water: 134 of the 277 canopy peaks inside the footprint lie over the traced water (99 in the north pond, most of them in its wooded east end, 35 in the south pond); each stands on a hummock, a hole of radius 1.6 m in the water round the peak (a bite out of the shore where the hole reaches it; holes closer than 3.2 m merge), simplified to 0.25 m with true-arc corners. The hummock's ground is the LiDAR's, filled in from round it (no ground returns under water), so it lies at or a few centimetres over the water; its size is a guess (UNVERIFIED). tools/evidence/trees.py keeps a tree that stands in a hole of the water. Not modelled: lily pads (white flecks over much of both ponds in the ortho), the outlet (none seen).
